data.label: Trigger New Opportunity
data.description: Start the workflow when a new sales opportunity is created in the CRM.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic event trigger based on a CRM record creation. No uncertainty, learning, or language understanding is required, so L0 is sufficient.

data.label: Validate Opportunity Fields
data.description: Check that the opportunity has an assigned owner, a stated dollar value, and a target close date.
data.rationale: This is pure rule-based validation of required fields. It can be implemented with if/then checks and data presence validation, so L0 is the correct level.

data.label: Fetch Historical Win Rate
data.description: Retrieve win-rate data for similar deals from historical CRM records.
data.rationale: This step is a data lookup against historical CRM records. It does not require ML or language processing; it can be handled deterministically via query/filter logic, so L0 is appropriate.

data.label: Assign Confidence Score
data.description: Calculate and store a deal-stage confidence score based on opportunity details and comparable historical outcomes.
data.rationale: Scoring based on historical outcomes suggests a statistical model or trained prediction function. L0 can compute a fixed formula, but using comparable historical data to assign a confidence score typically benefits from supervised ML, so L1 is the minimal appropriate level.

data.label: Evaluate High-Value Threshold
data.description: Determine whether the deal is high-confidence and above 50000 dollars.
data.rationale: This is straightforward deterministic threshold logic combining numeric comparison and a confidence flag. No AI is needed, so L0 is sufficient.

data.label: Schedule Proposal Prep Meeting
data.description: Automatically schedule a proposal-prep meeting with the sales engineering team for qualifying deals.
data.rationale: This step likely requires interacting with an external scheduling/calendar system and selecting an available meeting slot. The core action is orchestration plus API/tool use rather than pure logic, so L4 is appropriate.

data.label: Check Stall Duration
data.description: Determine whether the opportunity has stalled for more than 14 days without activity.
data.rationale: This is deterministic date arithmetic and activity-history checking. It can be handled with simple rules and timestamp comparisons, so L0 is sufficient.

data.label: Flag Manager Review
data.description: Flag the opportunity for sales manager review when stall conditions are met.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic CRM update/flagging action triggered by a rule condition. No learning or language capability is required, so L0 applies.

data.label: Draft Re-engagement Email
data.description: Create a re-engagement email draft for the rep to send to the stalled prospect.
data.rationale: Drafting an email requires language generation and tailored phrasing. A single LLM call can produce the draft without needing external tools, so L3 is appropriate.

data.label: Record Stage Transition
data.description: Log every stage transition with timestamp and triggering event in the CRM.
data.rationale: This is deterministic event logging with timestamp capture and metadata persistence. It is a classic L0 database write/audit trail operation.

data.condition: deal confidence is high and amount is greater than 50000

message: This workflow is mostly deterministic CRM automation (L0) with one ML-style scoring step (L1) and one language-generation step for the re-engagement email (L3). The scheduling step is tool-augmented orchestration (L4) because it likely requires external calendar/availability APIs. No multi-agent collaboration is required, so L5 is not needed.

workflow.workflowBrief: When a new sales opportunity is created in the CRM, verify that the deal has an assigned owner, a stated dollar value, and a target close date. Check the opportunity against historical win-rate data for similar deals and assign a deal-stage confidence score. For high-confidence deals above 50000 dollars, automatically schedule a proposal-prep meeting with the sales engineering team. For deals that have stalled more than 14 days without activity, flag the opportunity for sales manager review and draft a re-engagement email for the rep. Record every stage transition with timestamp and triggering event.
